entries.title: Romans 6:3
segments: Into his death. Into the death to sin obtained for the believer by Christ's voluntary sacrifice of himself.

entries.title: Romans 6:4
segments:
We were buried therefore, etc.  The apostle means to emphasize the idea that the true believer is so inseparably united by faith to Jesus Christ, the slain and risen Savior, that he shares both the grave and the resurrection glory with him.
 

 
Newness of life. A life free from the trammels and dangers of the old experience, even as the life of Christ after the resurrection was more free and glorious than his life on earth.

entries.title: Romans 6:6
segments: Our old man. Our old self.  Compare

The body of sin. The body considered as the instrument or servant of sin (

entries.title: Romans 6:7
segments: He that hath died. He who has died in Christ; he who has shared in Christ's death to sin.

entries.title: Romans 6:13
segments: As alive from the dead. As in the possession of eternal life.  See note on

entries.title: Romans 6:14
segments:
Not under law, but under grace. That is, under law in the wider sense of the term; any code of rules.
 

 
Under grace. In a state of acceptance with God; justified by faith.

entries.title: Romans 6:16
segments: Servants unto obedience. Servants who really obey.  The apostle takes his illustration from slavery, because only slavery, where the master has absolute power over the life and liberty of the slave, could here adequately represent the truth about man's position and dangers under the power of sin.  Each person must chose his or her master, must take a line of conduct which leads either to spiritual freedom (life), or spiritual slavery and denial of life (death).

entries.title: Romans 6:17
segments: That form of teaching, etc.  Their lessons in Christian faith and practice.  See

entries.title: Romans 6:19
segments:
I speak after the manner of men, etc.  The apostle illustrated the fact of the deliverance of the Corinthian Christians from sin by employing the language of the slave market, with which they were familiar.
 

 
Righteousness unto sanctification. The had chosen the right Master, Christ; let them now proceed, by growth in the spiritual life, unto sanctification.

entries.title: Romans 6:20
segments: Were free in regard of righteousness. In other words, they knew nothing about it.

entries.title: Romans 6:22
segments: Ye have your fruit unto sanctification, etc.  Paul here contrasts the shame and humiliation due to fleeting, sinful pleasures, with the blessedness and eternal life resulting from acceptance of Jesus Christ as the gift of God.
